name: Charismatic renewal

facts.value: 1960, among mainline Protestants in the U.S.

citations.excerpt: The charismatic movement, sometimes known as the charismatic renewal, began among mainline Protestants in the U.S. in 1960 and had spread to parts of the U.S. Catholic Church by 1967.

facts.value: Members of non-Pentecostal churches, including Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant, who hold some Pentecostal beliefs and practices such as healing, prophecy and speaking in tongues.

citations.excerpt: Charismatics are members of non-pentecostal denominations — including Catholic, Orthodox and some Protestant denominations — who hold at least some pentecostal beliefs and engage in at least some spiritual practices associated with pentecostalism, including divine healing, prophecy and speaking in tongues.
there are about 279 million pentecostal Christians and 305 million charismatic Christians in the world.

research_notes: Overlay. Influenced list is illustrative (Catholic, Anglican, Episcopal, ELCA); Pew names Catholic and mainline Protestants generally.
